description: The list of boundaries, holds and expected Ignore records that scripts/deploy-unit.ps1 applies, in the deploy gate and in the drift check (scripts/preflight-drift.ps1). A boundary is a field Azure owns, whose difference the gate accepts (inert) or stops on for a person (review). A hold is a resource the gate refuses to deploy unless the run names its ID in -AllowHeld. An expected Ignore is a live resource deliberately not declared in the unit that previews it, which the drift check accepts. Each entry carries its own reason. A what-if Modify passes the deploy gate only when every leaf delta is NoEffect or matches a boundary here. After the baseline deployment, a change named in -AllowModify (with -ApprovedChanges) passes too. An entry is added only when the evidence, such as a read-only preview, shows it is needed, never to make a gate pass.

matching.path: Delta paths are flattened to leaves and array indices are written as [*]. A pattern matches the path itself or anything below it (pattern followed by '.' or '['). '**' inside a pattern matches any run of characters.
matching.type: Resource type, case-insensitive, without API version.
matching.onDeploy: inert = the PUT does not send the value or the provider keeps the live value, so deploying changes nothing. review = the PUT sends a value that differs from live or its effect is unproven, so the gate stops unless the operator passes -AcknowledgeReview after reading the note.
matching.expectedIgnore: Live resources a unit deliberately does not write: existing references, resources declared in another unit, and resources another service creates. A deployment leaves Ignore records alone anyway (Incremental mode), but the drift check fails on any Ignore record that matches none of these patterns, except, in a subscription unit, a resource inside a group that has its own resource-group unit, which that unit measures. Each pattern names exact resources or the naming form the creating service uses (Azure for the network card of a private endpoint, GitHub for a runner card), so a resource created outside the code fails the check unless its name takes that form.
matching.holds: Resources the gate refuses to redeploy at all, whatever the what-if says, unless their IDs are passed in -AllowHeld. The drift sweep reports them but does not alert.

boundaries.reason: Provider response field on each zone config. A rewrite of the same zone group without it is accepted and leaves the A record untouched (same IP, TTL, id and record etag).

Provider response field. Azure gives the zone group a new etag on every write, so the code cannot carry it (declaring it gives NoChange once and a Modify after every write). A rewrite without it is accepted, as for id.

expectedIgnore.reason: The network card Azure creates for the private endpoint pe-kv-demo-mirror-secrets. Azure names it after the endpoint with a generated suffix and owns it, so the code does not declare it.

The identities and the secrets vault of rg-demo-identities. The unit demo-subscription writes the group and never what is in it, and a preview of the unit lists the contents as Ignore. They are declared in resource-groups/rg-demo-identities.deploy-excluded.bicep and previewed with parameters.verify.bicepparam.
